## 1. Goal

Build the hand-written, array-based binary heap that orders the waiting queue (by policy key) and the running set (by finish time). It is the central data structure of the engine and a core piece of the ADA content the viva examines.

## 2. Background

**From BLUEPRINT §3.1:**

An array-based binary heap that takes a compare function, so the same code serves the waiting queue (ordered by policy key) and the running set (ordered by finish time).

| Operation | Time |
| --- | --- |
| push | O(log n) |
| pop best | O(log n) |
| peek best | O(1) |
| build from array | O(n) |

Space is O(n). The heap is written by hand, not taken from a library, because showing it is part of the ADA content.

## 3. Scope

**In scope:**

- `core/heap.h` / `core/heap.c`: create, destroy, push, pop, peek, build, size
- Elements stored by value (fixed element size) or as pointers; ordering by a caller-supplied compare function with a context pointer
- Checked growth with `realloc`; no globals
- `tests/c/test_heap.c`

**Out of scope:**

- Policy compare functions (K-09, K-19)
- Decrease-key or delete-arbitrary (not needed: keys never change, BLUEPRINT §3.3)
- The engine (K-08)

## 5. Specification

Proposed interface (names may be refined in review; behaviour may not):

```c
/* Returns <0 if a should come out before b, >0 if after, 0 never for distinct jobs. */
typedef int (*HeapCmp)(const void *a, const void *b, void *ctx);

typedef struct {
    unsigned char *data;  /* elem_size * cap bytes, owned by the heap */
    size_t elem_size, len, cap;
    HeapCmp cmp;
    void *ctx;
} Heap;

int    heap_init(Heap *h, size_t elem_size, HeapCmp cmp, void *ctx);  /* APRM_OK or APRM_OUT_OF_MEMORY */
void   heap_free(Heap *h);                                            /* frees data; h reusable after init */
int    heap_push(Heap *h, const void *elem);                         /* O(log n) amortised */
int    heap_pop(Heap *h, void *out);                                 /* O(log n); APRM_INVALID_ARGUMENT if empty */
int    heap_peek(const Heap *h, void *out);                          /* O(1);     APRM_INVALID_ARGUMENT if empty */
int    heap_build(Heap *h, const void *elems, size_t n);             /* O(n) bottom-up heapify */
size_t heap_size(const Heap *h);
```

Costs required (BLUEPRINT §3.1): push O(log n), pop O(log n), peek O(1), build O(n), space O(n). Error codes used: `APRM_OUT_OF_MEMORY` (allocation failed; the heap is unchanged), `APRM_INVALID_ARGUMENT` (NULL pointer, zero element size, pop or peek on an empty heap). Every function has a comment: what it does, time and space complexity, who owns returned memory (`out` is caller-owned; `data` is heap-owned).

## 6. Step-by-step tasks

1. Write `heap.h` with the documented interface
2. Write tests for empty heap, single element and errors
3. Implement init/free/push with sift-up and doubling growth (checked `realloc`)
4. Implement pop/peek with sift-down
5. Implement build with bottom-up heapify
6. Add the 10,000-push random test for a min and a max compare
7. Run `make sanitize`

## 7. Tests to write

| Test name | What it checks | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_heap_empty` | pop and peek on an empty heap | Return `APRM_INVALID_ARGUMENT`, no crash |
| `test_heap_single` | push one, peek, pop | Same element back; size 0 after pop |
| `test_heap_random_min` | 10,000 random int64 pushes with a min compare | Pops come out in non-decreasing order |
| `test_heap_random_max` | Same with a max compare | Pops come out in non-increasing order |
| `test_heap_ties` | Equal primary keys with an id tie-break compare | Lower id first, every time |
| `test_heap_build` | build from 10,000 random elements, then pop all | Sorted output; same as pushing one by one |
| `test_heap_oom` | Allocator failure injected (test hook or tiny cap) | `APRM_OUT_OF_MEMORY`, heap still valid |
| `sanitize` | `make sanitize` on all heap tests | Zero AddressSanitizer/UBSan reports, no leaks |

## 10. Viva notes

**Idea:** a complete binary tree stored in an array; parent of i is (i−1)/2, children 2i+1 and 2i+2. Push adds at the end and sifts up; pop moves the last element to the root and sifts down.
**Invariant:** every parent compares before or equal to its children, so the best element is at index 0.
**Complexity:** height ⌊log₂ n⌋, so push/pop O(log n); peek O(1); bottom-up build O(n) because most nodes are near the leaves.
**Why a heap and not a sorted array?** O(log n) insert and remove versus O(n) insert (PRD §10A).
**Examiner question:** "Why is build O(n), not O(n log n)?" — Sum over levels of (nodes at that level × their height) is bounded by 2n.

## 11. Pitfalls

- Integer overflow in `cap * elem_size` when growing; check before multiplying
- Losing the old buffer when `realloc` fails (assign to a temporary first)
- Compare functions that return 0 for different jobs, making order platform-dependent
- Off-by-one in child index calculation
- Using `memcpy` with overlapping regions (use a temp swap buffer)
